newsitem.title: USA: Maine's June jobless rate eases to 4.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Maine's June jobless rate eases to 4.7 percent.

text.p: Maine's unemployment rate softened to 4.7 from 4.8 percent in June, reflecting a slight rise in hirings, the state Department of Labor said Tuesday.

The latest rate also marked an improvement from the year-ago level. "The Maine unemployment rate dropped over the past year from 5.3 percent in June 1996 to 4.7 percent in June 1997, representing a decline in the number of unemployed from 35,200 to 31,800," Valerie Landry, state Labor Commissioner, said in prepared remarks.

Nonfarm wage and salary employment rose by 1,400 between May and June, with increases in construction, services and government. Over the past year, nonfarm employment climbed by 7,200, mainly in services, construction and wholesale trade.

The state's unemployment rate fell in June to 4.5 percent from 4.7 percent, when seasonality was not accounted for, down from 5.0 percent a year-ago. Jobless rates by county ranged from 2.6 percent in Cumberland to 9.8 percent in Washington, when measured in this fashion.
